- cash_flow [fmp; fundamentals; per_study_asset; categories=["CashFlowStatements"]; window=required]: Capability: US/global company operating/investing/financing flows; issuer currency. Options: include_previous_observation indexBy reporting_period window.

- revenue_product_segmentation [fmp; fundamentals; per_study_asset; categories=["RevenueProductSegmentation"]; window=required]: Capability: Company product revenue by report date/segment; reportedCurrency. Options: include_previous_observation reporting_period window.

Asset screening uses complete native cohorts. Current loaded index keys: AEX25 ASX200 BIOTECH CAC40 DAX40 DJIA30 EUROSTOXX50 FTSE100 FTSEMIB40 FTSE_DEV_EXUS KOSPI200 MSCI_ACWI MSCI_CHINA MSCI_EAFE MSCI_EM MSCI_INDIA MSCI_JAPAN MSCI_WORLD NASDAQ100 NASDAQ_COMPOSITE NIKKEI225 R1000_GROWTH R1000_VALUE R2000_GROWTH R2000_VALUE RUSSELL1000 RUSSELL2000 RUSSELL3000 RUSSELL_MIDCAP SEMICONDUCTORS SMI20 SP1500 SP400 SP400_GROWTH SP500 SP500_COMM_SERVICES SP500_DISCRETIONARY SP500_ENERGY SP500_EQWT SP500_FINANCIALS SP500_GROWTH SP500_HEALTHCARE SP500_INDUSTRIALS SP500_MATERIALS SP500_REALESTATE SP500_STAPLES SP500_TECH SP500_UTILITIES SP500_VALUE SP600 SP600_VALUE SPTSX60 STOXX600 TSX_COMPOSITE US_TOTAL_MARKET. Native point-in-time-capable index keys: SP500 NASDAQ100 DOWJONES30. Set index_membership_mode explicitly to CurrentSnapshot or PointInTime. PointInTime needs a membership window and returns an overlap union; execution must still apply the native membership gate on each date. CurrentSnapshot uses the published current roster, even when an analysis window is historical. Missing source history remains an explicit error. Static catalog predicates and supported current-cap bounds belong in screen_assets. Computed ranks such as momentum belong in a study. max_assets is a fail-on-overflow guard, not top-k.

source.name: Cash Flow

options.name: Source Window
options.description: Required inclusive observation window for this source. Use SourceWindow(start=..., end=...), or bare StudyAssetPeriod when a Primary study_assets source exists. Bounds may use ISO dates, StudyAssetPeriodStart/End, DateBound(anchor=..., offset=<elapsed Duration>), or capability-gated EarliestAvailable/LatestAvailable.

options.name: Include Previous Observation
options.description: When true, prepend exactly one native source timestamp immediately before window.start for each source entity. Duplicate rows at that timestamp are preserved. No fill or carry is implied.

options.name: Reporting Period
options.description: Select financial statement reporting period: quarterly (10-Q), annual (10-K), or trailing_twelve_months (rolling sum of the most recent four quarters, served from FMP's /stable/cash-flow-statement-ttm).

options.name: Index By
options.description: Which date column becomes the DataFrame index. FilingDate is the default report-date coordinate, not an immutable publication vintage; AcceptanceDate currently retains only the SEC acceptance calendar date (the provider time is discarded); ObservationDate uses the fiscal period END (look-ahead when joined to price).

endpoint.description: Detailed cash flow statement for publicly traded companies (US and global). Use to analyze operating, investing, and financing cash flows for liquidity, capital allocation, and cash-conversion analysis. Indexed by fiscal report period end date; cadence (annual or quarterly) controlled by the request `period` argument. Money values are denominated in each issuer's `reportedCurrency`, not necessarily USD.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Fiscal report period end date — annual or quarterly per the request's `period` argument.

columns.name: reportedCurrency
columns.description: ISO 4217 currency code in which the figures are reported. Varies per issuer (USD for US filers, JPY for Toyota, EUR for SAP/ASML, etc.).

columns.name: cik
columns.description: SEC Central Index Key (zero-padded to 10 chars).

columns.name: acceptedDate
columns.description: SEC acceptance calendar date at day precision. FMP supplies `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`; the intraday component is intentionally discarded for now and the retained date is represented as `timestamp[ns,UTC]` at 00:00:00Z.

columns.name: period
columns.description: Reporting period — typical values: FY (annual), Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4.

columns.name: netCashProvidedByOperatingActivities
columns.display_name: Net Cash Provided By Operating Activities

columns.name: investmentsInPropertyPlantAndEquipment
columns.display_name: Investments In Property Plant And Equipment

columns.name: netCashProvidedByInvestingActivities
columns.display_name: Net Cash Provided By Investing Activities

columns.name: netCashProvidedByFinancingActivities
columns.display_name: Net Cash Provided By Financing Activities

columns.name: effectOfForexChangesOnCash
columns.display_name: Effect Of Forex Changes On Cash

columns.name: period_end_date
columns.description: Fiscal period-end date the statement COVERS (what the figures are ABOUT) — e.g. a Q1 statement covers the quarter ending ~Mar 31. Distinct from the filing/index date (when the report became public, weeks later). Group or label a fundamentals series by this to bucket values by fiscal period rather than by when they were disclosed.

columns.name: filing_date
columns.description: SEC filing date — when the report became publicly known. Equals the default point-in-time (FilingDate) index value, surfaced ALSO as a readable column so filing timing can be seen/compared alongside the fiscal period (period_end_date). Absent only for derived endpoints requested with indexBy=ObservationDate (the filing-date anchor is skipped in that look-ahead mode).

columns.name: accepted_date
columns.description: SEC acceptance calendar date at day precision (the AcceptanceDate index variant), represented as `timestamp[ns,UTC]` at 00:00:00Z. The provider intraday component is intentionally discarded for now. Present for primary statements and the synthesized FilingDate path; absent for derived endpoints requested with indexBy=ObservationDate.

source.name: Macrobond Vintage Data

options.name: Source Window
options.description: Required inclusive observation window for this source. Use SourceWindow(start=..., end=...), or bare StudyAssetPeriod when a Primary study_assets source exists. Bounds may use ISO dates, StudyAssetPeriodStart/End, DateBound(anchor=..., offset=<elapsed Duration>), or capability-gated EarliestAvailable/LatestAvailable.

options.name: Include Previous Observation
options.description: When true, prepend exactly one native source timestamp immediately before window.start for each source entity. Duplicate rows at that timestamp are preserved. No fill or carry is implied.

options.name: Series ID
options.description: Macrobond series identifier. Use mb_revision_info via the AI search service to confirm vintage availability before authoring — vintage depth varies dramatically (e.g. usnaac0001 has 138 captures back to 1991; long-tail series may have only 2-3 since 2021).

options.name: Revision
options.description: Which publication to reduce to. Always a FLAT series — one value per observation, indexed by that selected value's authentic publication instant. Last (default) = the latest-revised/final value; First = the advance/first-print; NthFromLast = an intermediate revision (see nth). Every view counts VALUE CHANGES, never snapshot republishes. First is served by the vendor's first-release record and OMITS observations that pre-date its vintage tracking (they have no first release); Last / NthFromLast keep those observations stamped release_kind=first_snapshot. No group_by + filter revision==1 by hand.

options.name: Nth From Last
options.description: Only used when revision=NthFromLast: how many REVISIONS back from the observation's last change to take (1 = the revision before the final value), released at that change's vintage. Counts value changes, not snapshot republishes. Clamped to the observation's debut, so a never-revised observation yields its debut row for every nth.

endpoint.description: Macrobond full revision tape for one series — every (vintage_date, observation_date, value) tuple Macrobond captured. Sort order = vintage_date ascending; within a vintage, observation_date follows the wire's order (typically chronological). Backbone of PIT-correct backtests: filter `vintage_date <= T` to reproduce the world's view at any past moment, group by observation_date and take last to get the latest-known value as-of T. Vintage tracking depth varies dramatically by series — major series like usnaac0001 go back to 1991 (138 vintages); long-tail series may have only 2-3 captures since 2021. Check `getRevisionInfo` first if depth matters. The previntage snapshot row (Macrobond's state at tracking-start) is dropped client-side because it has no real publish timestamp; for series Macrobond began tracking after their inception, pre-tracking-start observations are included only via the first real vintage's payload. Each row carries release_kind: whether its vintage_date is a live publication instant or the first-snapshot backfill stamp (ENG-1666).

columns.name: vintage_date
columns.description: Publication time of the row — the moment Macrobond captured this (observation_date, value) tuple from the upstream publisher. UTC instant with up-to-minute resolution from Macrobond's capture infrastructure (e.g., 2024-12-11T13:43Z = post-CPI release at 08:43 ET). The PIT axis: filter `vintage_date <= T` to get the world's view at time T. Note: the previntage row (Macrobond's snapshot at tracking-start) is dropped client-side because it has no real publish timestamp. For every observation already present when Macrobond began tracking the series this is the FIRST stored vintage's instant, not the observation's own publication time — see release_kind.

columns.name: observation_date
columns.description: The economic period the value describes (e.g., 2024-04-30 for April 2024 CPI). Stored as UTC midnight per the SDK's calendar-date convention (matches FMP's `date` field shape) — the timezone tag is bookkeeping, not a real instant. observation_date is a calendar period label, not a moment in time. One observation_date can appear under MANY vintage_dates: every revision republishes (or passes through) the same observation, so observation_date is NOT unique within the tape.

columns.name: value
columns.description: Observation value as published at vintage_date. Unit varies per series (currency, percent, count, index, ratio — check the series's Unit/Class metadata). Null means the source returned no observation for that period at that vintage. NaN/null values DO count as 'value present' for revision-counter purposes — null→null is a pass-through, null→number is a real revision.

columns.name: revision
columns.description: Per-observation_date revision counter — change-only. 1 = original publish (advance estimate in BLS terminology), 2 = first real revision (preliminary), 3 = second revision (final), etc. Pass-through vintages (Macrobond republished an unchanged value) DO NOT increment the counter — the value_changed flag distinguishes them. Query 'all 2nd revisions': `WHERE revision = 2 AND value_changed = true`.

columns.name: value_changed
columns.description: True when this row's value differs from the prior vintage's value for the same observation_date (covers real revisions and the debut row); false when Macrobond republished an unchanged value (no-op pass-through). Lets consumers separate 'the publisher actually moved this number' from 'the publisher confirmed the prior number stayed the same'.

columns.name: release_kind
columns.description: Whether release_date is timing evidence. `observed`: a live publication instant strictly after the series' first stored vintage. `first_snapshot`: the row was already present when Macrobond began tracking the series and inherited that first vintage's instant as its release_date — a backfill stamp, NOT when the observation was published; carries no timing evidence. `unknown`: no publication instant at all (fallback rows). Filter to `observed` before anchoring any event window on release_date. The first snapshot instant rides on the frame as schema metadata `epoch.macrobond.first_snapshot_time`.

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: The observation value under the selected `revision` view — first-print, latest-revised, or an intermediate vintage. One value per observation (the tape is reduced server-side). FIRST output, so a bare `mb_vintage_data(...)` reference resolves to the value; use `.release_date` / `.reference_date` for the bitemporal stamps. Unit varies per series (currency/percent/index/count/ratio — check the series Unit/Class metadata). Null where the source published no observation for that period at that vintage; ffill before joining to a denser bar series.

outputs.name: release_date
outputs.description: Full publication instant of the selected vintage (UTC, the knowledge timestamp), equal to the native index. For First this is the debut publication; for Last it is when the value was last revised. Use explicit `align` when combining it with another grid. NOT always a live publication time: rows already present when Macrobond began tracking the series carry the first stored vintage's instant (a backfill stamp) — read `release_kind` before treating this as event timing.

outputs.name: reference_date
outputs.description: The observation period the value covers (00:00 UTC). Pairs with the index to make each row bitemporal — reference_date is WHEN the data is about, the index/release_date is WHEN it became known (these differ by the publication lag, e.g. April data released in early May).

outputs.name: release_kind
outputs.description: Whether `release_date` is timing evidence for this row: `observed` (a live publication instant after the series' first stored vintage), `first_snapshot` (the row existed when Macrobond began tracking the series and inherited that vintage's instant — a backfill stamp with NO timing evidence), or `unknown` (no publication instant). Gate on `release_kind == "observed"` before anchoring any intraday or event window on `release_date`; never extrapolate a live row's time-of-day to first-snapshot rows. Verified on the US 20-year auction results: 57 of 78 rows are first_snapshot, 21 observed.

source.signature: x = mb_vintage_data(id, revision=First|Last|NthFromLast, nth=1, window=StudyAssetPeriod) — Macrobond vintage data over a REQUIRED explicit source window. RELEASE-INDEXED and bitemporal (same contract as te_calendar): the native index and `.release_date` retain the full publication instant, `.reference_date` is the observation period the value covers, and a bare reference / `.value` is the number. No daily-bar alignment is implicit. DEFAULT revision=Last = latest-revised/final (release_date = when last revised); revision=First = advance/first-print (released at debut); NthFromLast = `nth` revisions before the final value (default 1; counts value changes, clamped to the debut). First carries only observations with a vendor first-release record, so observations that pre-date Macrobond's vintage tracking are absent from First and present in Last as `release_kind=first_snapshot`. Reach for this only when you need MORE than te_calendar's first print — the revision dimension (first-vs-revised drift, an intermediate vintage). Vintage depth varies (headlines to ~1955, standard since ~2018, long-tail may be empty); confirm with mb_revision_info before authoring. Recipes: skill revision_tape, calendar_consensus_and_pit.

UTC instant with up-to-minute resolution from Macrobond's capture infrastructure (e.g., 2024-12-11T13:43Z = post-CPI release at 08:43 ET). The PIT axis: filter `vintage_date <= T` to get the world's view at time T. Note: the previntage row (Macrobond's snapshot at tracking-start) is dropped client-side because it has no real publish timestamp. For every observation already present when Macrobond began tracking the series this is the FIRST stored vintage's instant, not the observation's own publication time — see release_kind.

columns.name: observation_date
columns.description: The economic period the value describes (e.g., 2024-04-30 for April 2024 CPI). Stored as UTC midnight per the SDK's calendar-date convention (matches FMP's `date` field shape) — the timezone tag is bookkeeping, not a real instant. observation_date is a calendar period label, not a moment in time. One observation_date can appear under MANY vintage_dates: every revision republishes (or passes through) the same observation, so observation_date is NOT unique within the tape.

columns.name: value
columns.description: Observation value as published at vintage_date. Unit varies per series (currency, percent, count, index, ratio — check the series's Unit/Class metadata). Null means the source returned no observation for that period at that vintage. NaN/null values DO count as 'value present' for revision-counter purposes — null→null is a pass-through, null→number is a real revision.

columns.name: revision
columns.description: Per-observation_date revision counter — change-only. 1 = original publish (advance estimate in BLS terminology), 2 = first real revision (preliminary), 3 = second revision (final), etc. Pass-through vintages (Macrobond republished an unchanged value) DO NOT increment the counter — the value_changed flag distinguishes them. Query 'all 2nd revisions': `WHERE revision = 2 AND value_changed = true`.

columns.name: value_changed
columns.description: True when this row's value differs from the prior vintage's value for the same observation_date (covers real revisions and the debut row); false when Macrobond republished an unchanged value (no-op pass-through). Lets consumers separate 'the publisher actually moved this number' from 'the publisher confirmed the prior number stayed the same'.

columns.name: release_kind
columns.description: Whether release_date is timing evidence. `observed`: a live publication instant strictly after the series' first stored vintage. `first_snapshot`: the row was already present when Macrobond began tracking the series and inherited that first vintage's instant as its release_date — a backfill stamp, NOT when the observation was published; carries no timing evidence. `unknown`: no publication instant at all (fallback rows). Filter to `observed` before anchoring any event window on release_date. The first snapshot instant rides on the frame as schema metadata `epoch.macrobond.first_snapshot_time`.

# mb_vintage_data
Capability: Global macro/market selected vintages; release-indexed, native units.

RELEASE-INDEXED and bitemporal (same contract as `te_calendar`): the native index and `release_date` retain the full publication instant (the knowledge timestamp), `reference_date` carries the observation period the value covers, and `value` is the number. No daily-bar alignment is implicit. First = the advance/first-print (released at debut), Last = the latest-revised/final value (release_date = when it was last revised), NthFromLast = `nth` revisions before the final value (counts value changes, never snapshot republishes; clamped to the debut). First omits observations that pre-date the vendor's vintage tracking; Last / NthFromLast keep them as release_kind=first_snapshot. Study period bounds the series automatically.

Constructor: x = mb_vintage_data(id, revision=First|Last|NthFromLast, nth=1, window=StudyAssetPeriod) — Macrobond vintage data over a REQUIRED explicit source window. RELEASE-INDEXED and bitemporal (same contract as te_calendar): the native index and `.release_date` retain the full publication instant, `.reference_date` is the observation period the value covers, and a bare reference / `.value` is the number. No daily-bar alignment is implicit. DEFAULT revision=Last = latest-revised/final (release_date = when last revised); revision=First = advance/first-print (released at debut); NthFromLast = `nth` revisions before the final value (default 1; counts value changes, clamped to the debut). First carries only observations with a vendor first-release record, so observations that pre-date Macrobond's vintage tracking are absent from First and present in Last as `release_kind=first_snapshot`. Reach for this only when you need MORE than te_calendar's first print — the revision dimension (first-vs-revised drift, an intermediate vintage). Vintage depth varies (headlines to ~1955, standard since ~2018, long-tail may be empty); confirm with mb_revision_info before authoring. Recipes: skill revision_tape, calendar_consensus_and_pit.

Accepted named arguments: ["revision","nth","window","include_previous_observation"]

## mb_vintage_data_impl
Capability: Global macro/market selected vintages; release-indexed, native units.

RELEASE-INDEXED and bitemporal (same contract as `te_calendar`): the native index and `release_date` retain the full publication instant (the knowledge timestamp), `reference_date` carries the observation period the value covers, and `value` is the number. No daily-bar alignment is implicit. First = the advance/first-print (released at debut), Last = the latest-revised/final value (release_date = when it was last revised), NthFromLast = `nth` revisions before the final value (counts value changes, never snapshot republishes; clamped to the debut). First omits observations that pre-date the vendor's vintage tracking; Last / NthFromLast keep them as release_kind=first_snapshot. Study period bounds the series automatically.
mb_vintage_data_impl(window: SourceWindow, include_previous_observation: Boolean = false, series_id: String, revision: @VintageRevision = Last, nth: Int = 1 [1..])() → .value: Num, .release_date: Timestamp, .reference_date: Timestamp, .release_kind: String
- window: SourceWindow; required; step=0.000001. Required inclusive observation window for this source. Use SourceWindow(start=..., end=...), or bare StudyAssetPeriod when a Primary study_assets source exists. Bounds may use ISO dates, StudyAssetPeriodStart/End, DateBound(anchor=..., offset=<elapsed Duration>), or capability-gated EarliestAvailable/LatestAvailable.
- include_previous_observation: Boolean; optional; default=false; step=0.000001. When true, prepend exactly one native source timestamp immediately before window.start for each source entity. Duplicate rows at that timestamp are preserved. No fill or carry is implied.
- series_id: String; required; step=0.000001. Macrobond series identifier. Use mb_revision_info via the AI search service to confirm vintage availability before authoring — vintage depth varies dramatically (e.g. usnaac0001 has 138 captures back to 1991; long-tail series may have only 2-3 since 2021).
- revision: Select (VintageRevision); optional; default="Last"; choices=["First","Last","NthFromLast"]; step=0.000001. Which publication to reduce to. Always a FLAT series — one value per observation, indexed by that selected value's authentic publication instant. Last (default) = the latest-revised/final value; First = the advance/first-print; NthFromLast = an intermediate revision (see nth). Every view counts VALUE CHANGES, never snapshot republishes. First is served by the vendor's first-release record and OMITS observations that pre-date its vintage tracking (they have no first release); Last / NthFromLast keep those observations stamped release_kind=first_snapshot. No group_by + filter revision==1 by hand.
- nth: Integer; optional; default=1; minimum=1; step=0.000001. Only used when revision=NthFromLast: how many REVISIONS back from the observation's last change to take (1 = the revision before the final value), released at that change's vintage. Counts value changes, not snapshot republishes. Clamped to the observation's debut, so a never-revised observation yields its debut row for every nth.
Output value: Number. The observation value under the selected `revision` view — first-print, latest-revised, or an intermediate vintage. One value per observation (the tape is reduced server-side). FIRST output, so a bare `mb_vintage_data(...)` reference resolves to the value; use `.release_date` / `.reference_date` for the bitemporal stamps. Unit varies per series (currency/percent/index/count/ratio — check the series Unit/Class metadata). Null where the source published no observation for that period at that vintage; ffill before joining to a denser bar series.
Output release_date: Timestamp. Full publication instant of the selected vintage (UTC, the knowledge timestamp), equal to the native index. For First this is the debut publication; for Last it is when the value was last revised. Use explicit `align` when combining it with another grid. NOT always a live publication time: rows already present when Macrobond began tracking the series carry the first stored vintage's instant (a backfill stamp) — read `release_kind` before treating this as event timing.
Output reference_date: Timestamp. The observation period the value covers (00:00 UTC). Pairs with the index to make each row bitemporal — reference_date is WHEN the data is about, the index/release_date is WHEN it became known (these differ by the publication lag, e.g. April data released in early May).
Output release_kind: String. Whether `release_date` is timing evidence for this row: `observed` (a live publication instant after the series' first stored vintage), `first_snapshot` (the row existed when Macrobond began tracking the series and inherited that vintage's instant — a backfill stamp with NO timing evidence), or `unknown` (no publication instant). Gate on `release_kind == "observed"` before anchoring any intraday or event window on `release_date`; never extrapolate a live row's time-of-day to first-snapshot rows. Verified on the US 20-year auction results: 57 of 78 rows are first_snapshot, 21 observed.

## Fields: macrobond.series_fetch_all_vintage_series
Macrobond full revision tape for one series — every (vintage_date, observation_date, value) tuple Macrobond captured. Sort order = vintage_date ascending; within a vintage, observation_date follows the wire's order (typically chronological). Backbone of PIT-correct backtests: filter `vintage_date <= T` to reproduce the world's view at any past moment, group by observation_date and take last to get the latest-known value as-of T. Vintage tracking depth varies dramatically by series — major series like usnaac0001 go back to 1991 (138 vintages); long-tail series may have only 2-3 captures since 2021. Check `getRevisionInfo` first if depth matters. The previntage snapshot row (Macrobond's state at tracking-start) is dropped client-side because it has no real publish timestamp; for series Macrobond began tracking after their inception, pre-tracking-start observations are included only via the first real vintage's payload. Each row carries release_kind: whether its vintage_date is a live publication instant or the first-snapshot backfill stamp (ENG-1666).
Declared refresh: 01:30 Europe/Stockholm.
